name: PLA-CF
ams: All AMS models, including AMS Lite
notes: Matte finish, near-invisible layer lines, low warp. Support: 'Support for PLA New Edition'. Optional anneal 55–60 °C / 6–12 h for heat resistance.

name: PLA Sparkle
hardened: 0.4 mm hardened recommended (metal-particle filled) — no 0.2 mm
notes: Team purple with sparkle — the go-to for show parts. SKU 13700.
caution: Temps are color-specific and not confirmed on Bambu's first-party page; Bambu excludes Sparkle from the standard PLA spec row. Verify against the spool label.

name: PLA Plus
notes: Bulk white workhorse. No official slicer profile — use Generic PLA.
caution: We also stock ELEGOO RAPID PLA+ (its own row below) — a different SKU with different temps. Check which box you picked up before copying settings.

name: Premium PLA Plus
notes: Print speed 40–80 mm/s. No official slicer profile — Generic PLA.

name: PLA PRO (PLA+)
notes: PrusaSlicer has a built-in 'eSUN PLA' preset that works acceptably — occasionally stringy for PLA+. No Bambu Studio built-in.

name: Tough Pro PLA+
notes: The only filament we stock with an official brand-provided profile in BOTH Bambu Studio (all printers, 4 nozzle sizes) and PrusaSlicer. ~4.3× the impact toughness of standard PLA, heat resistance closer to ABS. 100% virgin NatureWorks Ingeo, no fillers.

name: RAPID PLA+
drying: Low need; ships vacuum-sealed with desiccant
notes: High-speed PLA+ — the box rates it 30–600 mm/s. Temps above are off the box label (code 1-2503-0321).
caution: This is the line the plain ELEGOO PLA Plus row warns about — we own BOTH. Read the box before copying settings between them.

name: PLA+
notes: Made in USA. Two colorways on the shelf: a Blue spool (barcode 850032116169) and a boxed Light Blue (barcode 700512752588). Temps above are off the spool label; IIID MAX publishes a narrower 190–220 °C / 55–70 °C for the standard PLA+.
caution: Our spools are not marked "HS", so the reorder link (High Speed PLA+) may not be the exact SKU — check the label before assuming the 300 mm/s speed rating.

name: PETG-CF
ams: Standard, AMS Lite, and AMS 2 Pro
notes: One of only two CF filaments that run in AMS Lite (with PLA-CF). Glossier than PLA-CF and hides layer lines. Support: Bambu Support for PLA/PETG. Speed <200 mm/s, fan 0–40%.

name: PET-CF
ams: Standard yes · Lite no · AMS HT best for drying
notes: 0.6 mm nozzle recommended, speed ≤100 mm/s. Not compatible with the 0.2 mm stainless nozzle or Bambu Liquid Glue.
caution: A DIFFERENT product from PETG-CF above — different base resin (PET vs PETG) and ~40 °C hotter. Don't swap the profiles.

name: PETG-GF
drying: Not published — dry as a standard PETG precaution
notes: Speed <220 mm/s. Not in Bambu Studio's built-in list — start from Generic PETG.

name: PETG
notes: No slicer profile — Generic PETG. Community speed 25–37 mm/s.
caution: Bed temp sources conflict (one says 70–85 °C). Confirm against the spool label.

name: Carbon Fiber PETG (PETG-CF)
drying: Not published — treat as PETG, 65 °C / 6–8 h if it strings
ams: Not recommended — abrasive CF, feed from an external spool
notes: 20 % chopped carbon fiber. Manufacturer calls for a 0.4 mm minimum nozzle (0.6 mm+ ideal), 30–60 mm/s (40 recommended), and fan 0 % on layer 1 ramping to 50 % from layer 5.

name: Hard TPU 72D
ams: AMS-fed in the lab — cap volumetric flow at 6 mm³/s
notes: Shore 72D — much stiffer than 95A TPU; bendable but not stretchy. Speed 30–40 mm/s, retraction 0–4 mm. Start from Generic TPU / Bambu TPU-95A.

name: TPE-83A
ams: NOT AMS-safe — documented jams; needs direct-drive + external spool holder
notes: Softer and stretchier than TPU. Speed <50 mm/s, 100% part-cooling fan. A sizzling sound while printing means the filament is wet.
caution: No Bambu Studio profile exists for this material on any machine -- confirmed against the vendor bundle. It is also much softer than the 95A TPU family profile, so that family will feed it badly. Mentor-only, hand-tuned settings.

name: TPU 95A
drying: Dry if it has been open a while
notes: Speed 25–40 mm/s. No official slicer profile.
caution: Only the nozzle temp is brand-confirmed — bed, speed, and drying figures are generic TPU guidance, not HATCHBOX's own spec.

name: TPU
drying: Dry before use despite vacuum sealing
notes: Speed 20–30 mm/s. No slicer profile.
caution: Known to print undersized — a verified buyer reports needing ~112% extrusion multiplier. Shore hardness (~95A) is unconfirmed for this exact SKU. Print a test cube and measure before committing to a real part.

name: Fibreheart TPU-GF
ams: AMS and AMS Lite yes — NOT AMS 2
notes: Official Bambu Studio profiles exist for X1C/P1S/A1/H2D/H2S/X2D and more, plus OrcaSlicer — download from siraya.tech/pages/print-settings-download. No native PrusaSlicer profile. Speed 30–100 mm/s.
caution: Glass-fiber dust: N95+ mask and goggles when sanding or machining printed parts. No Bambu Studio profile exists for TPU-GF on any machine -- confirmed against the vendor bundle. Mentor-only, hand-tuned settings until one exists.

name: CoexFlex TPU 60A
drying: Dry 50–55 °C / 6–8 h if it bubbles or strings
ams: No — far too soft; direct drive, external spool only
notes: Made in the USA. COEX calls for a direct-drive extruder with a fully constrained filament path and a PTFE-lined hotend; start at 20 mm/s and work up to about 40.
caution: Softest flexible we own, and it breaks down above 230 °C. It will jam a Bowden path and an AMS — direct-drive machines only.

name: Pneumatique (recycled-tyre TPE)
notes: Thermoplastic elastomer compounded with rubber recovered from recycled car tyres — about 80 Shore A, matte grey-black with a faintly rough, anti-grip "tyre" texture. Print 20–40 mm/s.
caution: Smells strongly of rubber while printing — run the enclosure exhaust. The spool label lists only colour, diameter and weight, so the bed temperature here is our estimate, not a TreeD spec.

name: INNOVATEFIL TPU-CF
ams: No — flexible and abrasive; external spool
notes: Shore 67D — a rigid flexible, the closest thing on the shelf to the 72D house TPU. The carbon fiber also makes it ESD-dissipative.

name: TPU 95A
nozzle: Not on the label — 210–230 °C is the usual 95A window
notes: Same job as the HATCHBOX TPU 95A already on the shelf — burn the two down together rather than opening both.
caution: No temperatures printed anywhere on the spool. The values here are the generic 95A window, not a manufacturer spec — run a temp tower before a long print.

name: PPA-CF
hardened: Required — 0.6 mm first choice, no 0.2 mm
ams: NOT AMS-compatible (any model) — external spool holder only
notes: Higher modulus and strength than PAHT-CF — a different resin family (PPA vs PA12), not a rename. Speed <100 mm/s. No dedicated Bambu support product; use ABS/ASA as interface.
caution: Carbon dust — wear gloves when handling and cleaning up.

name: PAHT-CF
ams: Standard AMS and AMS HT yes · AMS Lite no
notes: The successor to the discontinued 'PA-CF' — when older docs say PA-CF, this is what they mean. Remove supports within ~2 h of printing; moisture swelling makes them stick.
caution: Carbon dust hazard. Bambu's 'Support for PA/PET' is discontinued — use ABS or ASA as the interface material.

name: Fibreheart PPA-CF
enclosure: Mandatory per manufacturer — explicitly not for A1/A1 mini
notes: Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer, AND native PrusaSlicer (XL/MK4S/Core One) profiles available. Fan off. Speed 30–120 mm/s.
caution: Do not confuse with Siraya's 'PPA-CF Core' 25%-CF variant — different product. AMS compatibility is reported inconsistently across sources; treat as external-spool-only until Siraya confirms.

name: Fibreheart PPA-GF
ams: Explicitly NOT compatible — but see notes: we run it through the H2D's AMS HT anyway (declared as Bambu PA6-GF)
notes: Bambu Studio + OrcaSlicer profiles at siraya.tech/pages/print-settings-download. Fan off. Speed 30–100 mm/s, first layer 20–30. In practice we load it in the H2D's AMS HT by declaring the slot as Bambu PA6-GF — Bambu's own glass-fiber nylon profile, a closer material match than the carbon-fiber PAHT-CF profile we tried first — then manually override nozzle to 310 °C, chamber to 60–80 °C, and drying to 80–100 °C / 4–6 h. H2D only: the X1Cs and the X2D both cap their hotends at 300 °C, short of the 310 °C this needs. Do NOT declare it as Bambu PPA-CF: that profile is itself flagged non-AMS-compatible (any model) and may cause the AMS HT to refuse the load.
caution: Manufacturer explicitly recommends an N95+ respirator and HEPA/carbon ventilation for printing AND post-processing. Run it in the enclosed printer with the vent on.

name: PA-Alloy 910
bed: 45–65 °C on glass + PVA, BuildTak + PVA, or PEI
notes: Highest tensile strength in taulman's nylon lineup (~56 MPa, 8,100+ PSI), elongation 31–32%. Lower water absorption than their other nylons. Pick this for mechanical linkages. Fan off, retraction 3–4 mm.
caution: taulman3d.com is dead/domain-squatted — specs come from a reseller. Drying guidance from third parties is inconsistent (3 h/150 °C to '8 h/82 °C insufficient'); dry longer rather than shorter. The nearest Bambu Studio profile is Generic PA-CF, a carbon-filled nylon -- this spool is unfilled, so flow and shrinkage will differ even though the temperature band overlaps enough to print. Confirm on a real print before trusting it for a part that matters.

name: Nylon PA 'Cast Plate'
drying: Dry before every session — re-absorbs humidity within ~18 h of opening
notes: 'Cast Plate' is a filament grade emulating industrial cast nylon plate (~95 MPa tensile, HDT 112 °C / 185 °C annealed) — not a bundled bed accessory. Hotter than taulman's 645/680 nylons. Speed 38–40 mm/s, fan off.
caution: Never use nylon as support for nylon — it welds permanently. Use taulman SAC1060 breakaway (235–255 °C) or PVA; not HIPS. Bed figure not confirmed on a live taulman page (domain dead). The nearest Bambu Studio profile is Generic PA-CF, a carbon-filled nylon -- this spool is unfilled, so flow and shrinkage will differ even though the temperature band overlaps enough to print. Confirm on a real print before trusting it for a part that matters.

name: PCTPE (Nylon/TPE co-polymer)
notes: taulman's most flexible nylon — elongation 370–497%, tensile 35 MPa. For wearables, vibration damping, and grips. Fan off, ~30–50 mm/s.
caution: The flexible outlier in the taulman family — not a strength competitor to Alloy 910. Shore hardness (~D45) is estimated, not manufacturer-verified. taulman3d.com is dead; specs are reseller-sourced. No Bambu Studio profile exists for this nylon/TPE co-polymer on any machine -- confirmed against the vendor bundle. Mentor-only, hand-tuned settings.

name: PA-CF (nylon carbon fiber)
spool: 750 g — a sealed case of 5 plus loose spools
drying: 80–100 °C / 8–12 h before every print after the first; print from a heated dry box
ams: No — abrasive and hygroscopic; external dry box
notes: About 89 % polyamide with 10 % chopped carbon fiber; HDT around 178 °C. Spool label calls for 30–60 mm/s. Case part FIL001301750175, batch 2-191203, lot 2-191106.
caution: Old stock — the case carries 2019 lot numbers. Nylon pulls moisture through packaging over that long; run a full dry cycle before the first print or expect popping and a furry surface.

name: PC
enclosure: REQUIRED — not compatible with open-frame printers
ams: Standard and AMS HT yes · Lite no
notes: Speed <300 mm/s. No dedicated Bambu support product for plain PC.
caution: High fumes — run it in an enclosed printer with ventilation, not on an open bench.

name: PC
drying: ~20 h at 70 °C on first use — extremely hygroscopic
notes: No slicer profile — use Bambu Studio's Generic PC with chamber ~60 °C. Speed 30–50 mm/s.
caution: Speed and the higher temp range are community-reported, not datasheet values. High odor — ventilate.

name: PC-CF
notes: Fan off or ≤20%, 10 mm brim recommended. No slicer profile — Generic PC-CF, or Generic PC with the hardened-nozzle flag. Speed ~40–50 mm/s.
caution: A Prusa forum thread reports inconsistent spool quality from this brand — spot-check a spool before trusting it on a competition part. No Bambu Studio profile exists for PC-CF on any machine we own -- confirmed against the vendor bundle. Start from the plain PC profile and expect to hand-tune; mentor-only until it has a real profile.

name: Prusament PC Blend Carbon Fiber
spool: 800 g net (871 g with spool) — 2 sealed boxes
enclosure: Recommended — PCCF warps far less than plain PC, but our enclosed machines are the safe default
notes: SKU PRM-PCB-CFB-800. Heat resistance about 114 °C, or 130 °C annealed. Prusa recommends a powder-coated or satin textured sheet for adhesion. Each box carries a Prusament spool ID you can look up at prusament.com for that spool’s measured diameter.
caution: Made December 2021 — years in storage. Dry it before use.

name: PPS-CF
drying: 100–140 °C / 8–12 h in a blast oven — the box says 120 ± 10 °C, 6–8 h
hardened: Required — hardened steel, bimetal or tungsten carbide; not compatible with the 0.2 mm stainless hotend
ams: No — not compatible with any AMS
notes: The hottest material in the building. Higher values in the nozzle range improve Z-direction strength. Optional anneal at 180–220 °C for 6–12 h.
caution: Needs a hotend over 300 °C AND a heated chamber -- H2D only. Bambu ships no PPS-CF profile for the X2D at all (confirmed against the vendor bundle), so it cannot be sliced there no matter what the machine can physically reach; not a policy choice, a hard gap. Most of the rest of the fleet cannot run it either.

name: Polypropylene, glass-filled
enclosure: Effectively required (PP warps and shrinks badly)
notes: Print surface matters more than usual: PP packing tape or a PP-specific sheet — PP barely sticks to anything but itself, and glue stick will not save you. Support: PP-based only; PLA/PETG supports bond poorly. Speed 30–60 mm/s.
caution: Generic listing with no manufacturer page. Whether the 'glass filled' claim is real fiber reinforcement could not be verified — inspect the spool before assuming a hardened nozzle is or isn't needed. Bed temp is general PP guidance, not listing-specific.

name: Support for PA/PET
ams: Standard and AMS HT yes · Lite no
notes: Was the correct support interface for PAHT-CF, PA6-CF, PA6-GF, and PET-CF.
caution: DISCONTINUED by Bambu. If any spools remain on the shelf, use them up; going forward Bambu recommends ABS or ASA as the support interface for PA/PET prints.

name: Support W (Support for PLA)
notes: Breakaway support interface for PLA only — set the support Z distance to 0 in Bambu Studio so the interface peels off clean, which is exactly the zero-gap interface job the materials policy keeps PLA around for. Not water-soluble.
caution: Not interchangeable with the Support for PA/PET (Support G) already on the shelf — that one is for the hot materials, this one only works under PLA.
